## p164a — Occupation army, Temesvar and MIRCO fragments

**Edition context:** p164a — Damaged Temesvar and MIRCO fragments.

<a id="edition-cases-p164a-p164a--damaged-temesvar-and-mirco-fragments"></a>



This damaged Nov7–9-key message contains a proposed reference to an occupation army at Temesvar and to routes west and south of `MIRCO`. Our new reading **BESATZUNGSHEER** agrees with all eighteen observed coordinate halves in positions 18–31. Its ten mask fills change no observed coordinate; the word also occurs in independently decoded p66 and p115 messages.

| Reading layer | Fixed positions | Observed substitutions | Mask fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Source alone | 42/121 | 0 | 0 |
| New occupation-army word | 52/121 | 0 | 10 |
| New word with Norbert's date/place proposal | 60/121 | 1 | 20 |
| Revised combined proposal, including earlier conjectural clauses | 104/121 | 4 | 66 |

The [revised certificate](../../experiments/p164_occupation_fragment/README.md) gives each layer separately. The former combined proposal fixed 101 positions with five substitutions and 63 fills.

**Readable German — date and occupation-army excerpt; surrounding text remains incomplete:**

> […] 9.11. Temesvar. Besatzungsheer […]

The date and place retain Norbert's earlier proposal, supported by the independently received p153 A3 ending. Together with the new word they recover a coherent fragment; the intervening military designations and the later route clause still require work.

**Readable German — earlier conjectural fragments; display omissions are not counted positions:**

> […] [in Temesvar] […] [die von MIRCO nach Westen und Sueden … Wege … vom Gegner besetzt]. […]

**Meaning:** The earlier reconstruction refers to Temesvar and appears to report enemy occupation of routes west and south of `MIRCO`. The central clause and its grammar remain unresolved; a later suggestion reads `DIV VON MIRCO` instead of `DIE VON MIRCO`.

These bracketed clauses come from Norbert's 2017 proposal. Their grammar and the identity of `MIRCO` remain unresolved. The new occupation-army word replaces his earlier `BEFRIEDNISXE??` span; the complete revised stream is linked above.

## p164 A4 — Dismounted cavalry west of an unidentified MIRCO

**Edition context:** p164 A4 — cavalry report.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p164-a4-p164-a4--cavalry-report"></a>



**Status:** Conditional editorial reconstruction of a contextual sibling, outside the 22-target challenge. **Contribution:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. It does not change the partial status of [p164a](#edition-cases-p164a) or [p164b](#edition-cases-p164b).

<a id="edition-cases-context-p164-a4-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Vorstoss der abgesessenen 4./1. G. Drag. stiess westl. MIRCO auf staerkeren Gegner. MIRCO wurde vom Gegner besetzt.

**Meaning:** An advance by dismounted cavalry met stronger opposition west of `MIRCO`; `MIRCO` was occupied by the enemy.

**Notes:** The entire sentence is an editorial reconstruction requiring **nine known-coordinate substitutions and thirteen erasure fills**. The nine printed glyphs were independently rechecked and support the literal transcription. These proposed changes therefore alter historical source evidence. `MIRCO` remains unidentified; it is not silently replaced by `MIROC` or a modern place name.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p164-a4-source-reading"></a>

### Source reading

The source has 198 coordinate slots, including 13 erasures, although its header advertises 188. Under the audited 7–9 November key, with no repairs, **87 of 99 plaintext characters are fixed**:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VORG?OSSDX?A?GESESSEK?NX4X1XGXD?AGXGTIESSWES?LX?IRCOAUFGTAER0EREFGEGNERX?IY?OWURDE?OMGEGNER??SETSTX
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-context-p164-a4-unit-interpretation"></a>

### Unit interpretation

Expanding `4./1. G. Drag.` as the 4th Squadron of the 1st Guard Dragoon Regiment is a contextual inference. The unit is attested in the US War Department's [1920 divisional history, p689](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/55620/55620-h/55620-h.htm#Page_689), under the 218th Division: its 1917 column names the Guard Dragoon regiment, while its 1918 column omits “Guard.” This association does not verify the wording or locate the squadron on the intercept date.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p164-a4-exact-edit-certificate"></a>

### Exact edit certificate

All indices below are zero-based positions in the original 198-slot source.

| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |

| 51 | V | X | K → N in ABGESESSENEN |

Erasure fillings are `1:G, 7:A, 8:G, 9:D, 14:A, 50:A, 61:D, 68:G, 69:G, 73:G, 141:V, 142:D, 176:D`. No coordinate is inserted or deleted.

```

</details>

AGXXDXAAGDDDVGAXDADGFDVDDDDFDGVVVXDDVDVXGVGXVVGXXGAXXDFVAXAFXDAAFDVDGGDVVGXXAADDDFGVGDFDDVXGVGVGVGVDXGDVDDFAVADGVXDGDVDXVGVVVVXVFVVAVVXGDFVXDVDXXVVVXDDVDDADGFDXXVGFDGXGVXXVXDXGDGVDDVDAADADXDDDGDXAXV
```

An eight-substitution alternative omits the change at source 179 and leaves source 50 erased. It therefore reads `VORSTOSSDX?ABGESESSENEN...`, with the remaining plaintext character restricted to `02ACLR`. The certificate retains all six conditional completions.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p164-a4-what-this-changes"></a>

### What this changes

The source fragment `A?GESESSEK?N` can be reconstructed as `ABGESESSENEN` with one known-coordinate substitution and three erasure fills. Consequently, its internal `ESSEK` substring is not sufficient evidence for identifying Osijek. MIRCO remains unidentified; no geographic substitution or expansion is adopted. The apparent height 828 in part 5 does not determine the interpretation.

The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p164_A4_editorial.json) and [standalone verifier](../../adfgvx/editorial164.py) reproduce the raw reading, each explicit edit, all six partial completions, and the complete proposed plaintext's re-encryption. The verifier uses coordinate arithmetic only. Successful verification confirms the consequences of the proposed edits, not their historical truth.

```sh
python3 -m adfgvx.editorial164
```

Source: [Childs p164](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p164_ACD.png).

<a id="edition-cases-context-p164-a4-geographic-lead"></a>

### Geographic lead

[The geographic review](../../data/reviews/p164_geography.json) records Martin's 1920 regimental history: on 24 October it places twenty men of a closely matching 4th Squadron/1st Prussian Dragoon designation at Mosnac, near the later Miroc fighting. Its subsequent chronology and the different report date prevent a firm identification. Changing both `MIRCO` occurrences to `MIROC` would additionally alter three known source coordinates and one guessed fill. No such normalization is adopted. The relevant French daily journal is identified as an archive lead, with its entries still uninspected.

## p164 B — Dismantle the station and resume calls after reaching Temesvar

**Edition context:** p164 B — Dismantling the station and marching to Temesvar.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p164-b-p164-b--dismantling-the-station-and-marching-to-temesvar"></a>



**Status:** 69/70 raw positions fixed; two explicit coordinate substitutions
in the readable edition; one time digit remains conditional. **Source edition
and review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. **Period key:** George Lasry and
colleagues.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p164-b-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German — both unresolved time-cell alternatives retained:**

> Wir abbauen 9.11., [05:00 oder 06:00], Weitermarsch Temesvar. Wenn dort aufgebaut,
> rufen wir.

**Display notes:** This readable German includes the two recorded repairs below and keeps both time alternatives. The bracketed whole field is an alternative display of the single unassigned digit in `0?00`; the colon is editorial punctuation. It does not select the later historical `05:00` interpretation.

**Meaning:** The station will be dismantled, followed by an onward march to
Temesvar; it will call again once set up there. The literal cipher-only time is
05:00 or 06:00. Under the already documented historical completion of the
7–9 November square, it is **05:00 on 9 November**.

The telegram style is retained; *wir bauen ab* is the ordinary German wording.
The proposed month `11` repairs the raw `18`. The proposed `RUFEN` repairs raw
`RUDEN`. Both changes are individually costed below.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p164-b-source"></a>

The source marker is printed `RIZI`, not silently normalized to `RICHI`.

The unknown plaintext position 17 is the square cell `XA`, whose baseline

| Proposed correction | Plaintext position | Received-coordinate change |

All indices are zero-based. The source header supports the November reading;
the verb is a language-based repair. There are **two known-coordinate

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p164-b-conditional-time-digit"></a>

### Conditional time digit

The existing
[historical square layer](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
gives `VF=6`, `XA=5`, from the independently identified 6th Reserve Division.
Using that same global square assigns `XA=5` here and gives `0500` without any
additional ciphertext change. The baseline square and its `{5,6}` alternative
remain intact. Accepting the date and verb repairs does not require accepting
this separate historical inference.

The proposed edition under that layer is:

**Conditional interpretation — two coordinate repairs plus the separate historical XA = 5 hypothesis:**

```text
WIRXABBAUEN9X11X0500WEITERMARSCHXTEMESVARXWENNDORTAUFGEBAUTXRUFENXWIRX
```

It re-encrypts exactly to the two-substitution ciphertext.

## p164 C1 — AOK11 evening report: Danube crossing and Belgrade–SEMUM traffic

**Edition context:** 9 November: Danube report and Arad provisions.

**Related source pages:** [p168 E](168.md#source-p168-e).

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-november-9-danube-report-and-arad-provisions"></a>



These reports received on 9 November concern a Danube crossing and provisions at Arad for **80,000 men and 30,000 animals**. Source comparison restores a misread Danube-report glyph and eleven coordinates missing from the earlier Arad copy. The readings use the published **Nov7–9** key.

<a id="source-p164-c1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-p164-c1"></a>

### p164 C1

**Readable German — conditional date and army completion:**

> AOK11. Abendmeldung 8.11.18. Lage der 11 Armee am 7.11 abends. Donauuebergang 219 I D beendet. Belgrad SEMUM. Lebhafter Uebersetzverkehr.

This first part of a five-part report describes the Eleventh Army's evening situation on 7 November: the 219th Infantry Division has completed its Danube crossing, with busy crossing traffic at `BELGRAD` and `SEMUM`. The proposed report date is 8 November 1918; interception followed early on 9 November. `SEMUM` retains the transmitted spelling.

The completion reads `8XC1X1?` as a day.month.year date and identifies `?1 ARMEE` with the `AOK11` already named at the start. The nearby [p155 report](155.md#edition-cases-military-nov7-derailment-and-trains-p155-d) uses the fully observed date form `7X11X18`. These two contextual assumptions complete **124/124 positions** at a total cost of **five observed substitutions and five source-mask fills**.

| Field | Additional source changes, zero-based | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `8XC1X1?` → `8X11X18` | 139 `D` → `G`; 164 dash → `A` | Day.month.year interpretation within the 1918 sequence |
| `?1 ARMEE` → `11 ARMEE` | 52 invalid `C` → `G` | The same message opens with native `AOK11` |

Literal header: `C) ZON v UKS (1.57 a.m., November 9th); 2101 5 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-248`. [Source crop](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/sources/p164_C1.png).

<summary>p164 source, earlier word layer and exact conditional completion</summary>

parallel p153 passage raise this to 121 before lexical repair. The earlier
word proposal costs four observed substitutions and three printed-mask fills,
leaving the date and army fields unresolved:

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 reference interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies **6** in the Arad footer, giving **RM 1C 186 GEH** and **136/136 conditional edited labels** in p168 E. The opposite assignment gives 185 GEH. Both coordinates of this VF pair are original observations. The four word substitutions, two printed-mask fills and one supplied gap coordinate remain unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-arad-cross-copy-restoration"></a>

### Arad cross-copy restoration

The p168 witness raises the earlier p159 primary frame from **124 to 135 fixed positions**. Its eleven supplied coordinates are all directly observed in p168, independent of the three values p168 borrows in the reverse comparison. This establishes the formerly uncertain strength field from surviving source pairs.

<details>
<summary>Restored p159 stream and complete source-family comparison</summary>

**Raw output — p159 primary geometry with all 11 missing coordinates supplied from observed p168 pairs:**

```text
0NOHLXVERPOLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEX10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXEUEGENACHARADXARADNEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE80000MANNX30000TISREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GLHX
```

The coordinate-only comparison covers 173,580 canonical layouts and 694,320
source-origin maps. Five disagreements across 258 jointly observed positions
are the minimum. Only two canonical layouts remain: short-slot boundary 118
with five-slot boundaries (15,110) or (16,110). The four choices of duplicated
group origin give eight minimizing maps, all with one completed ciphertext
and 135/136 fixed labels. Each supplies its eleven additions from native
p168 observations.

Within this error family, coordinate comparison reduces the earlier 64 word-conditioned minima to eight and excludes all 48 P0000 alternatives. The earlier six-change objective fitted a word template; the present five-disagreement objective compares the received coordinates.

</details>

The common edited reading costs **seven observed substitutions in p159**
and **four in p168**. The extra p159 repair beyond its earlier six-word layer
adopts p168’s GEH footer spelling. Both copies keep the globally coupled
unknown digit. The [current p159 case](159.md#edition-cases-military-arad-provisions-partial) now presents
this improved collation first, with the superseded U and P0000 hypotheses
in a historical comparison drawer.
